questions.question: Dr Samia must choose between stereolithography (SLA) and DLP for 3D printing. What is the main difference between these two technologies?
options: SLA uses a laser, DLP uses a projector
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'SLA uses a laser beam to polymerize the resin point by point, while DLP projects a complete image of the layer at once.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid wants to print surgical guides. Which 3D printing technology is best suited for this application?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'SLA and DLP offer the precision and surface quality required for surgical guides.'

questions.question: Dr Samia has printed a resin model for an orthodontic aligner. Dr Rachid asks her to check the accuracy. What is the acceptable tolerance?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'The acceptable tolerance for an aligner model is 0.1 mm to guarantee an optimal clinical result.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must choose a resin for printing surgical guides. Which characteristic is the most important?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Biocompatibility and sterility are essential for surgical guides that will be in contact with the patient's tissues.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must manage a 3D printing failure. Dr Rachid explains the possible causes. What is the most frequent cause?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Printer calibration is the most frequent cause of 3D printing failure.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must print several surgical guides in a single session. What is the best organization strategy?
options: Print one guide at a time
Optimize the placement of parts on the platform
Use a different printer for each guide
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Optimizing the placement of parts on the platform maximizes printing efficiency.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must choose between standard resin and specific dental resin. What is the major difference?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Specific dental resins are formulated to be biocompatible and meet the mechanical requirements of dental applications.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must print models for orthodontic aligners. What surface quality is required?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'A smooth and precise surface is essential for the manufacture of orthodontic aligners.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must manage a case of deformed printed model. Dr Rachid asks her to check a critical parameter. What is this parameter?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'The printer temperature can influence the deformation of printed models.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must print a surgical guide with metal sleeves. What is the best approach?
options: Print the guide with integrated sleeves
Print the guide and add the sleeves after
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'The best approach is to print the guide and add the metal sleeves after to guarantee their precise positioning.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must train her assistant in post-processing of 3D printed parts. What is the essential post-processing step?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Cleaning and drying are essential to remove resin residues and ensure the precision of the part.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid has printed a surgical guide. Dr Samia asks him to check the sterilization. What is the recommended sterilization method?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Ethylene oxide is the recommended sterilization method for resin-printed surgical guides.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must choose a slicing software for her 3D printer. Which criterion is the most important?
options: Compatibility with the printer and the quality of parameters
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Compatibility and parameter quality are essential for obtaining quality prints.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must manage a 3D printer that produces parts with surface defects. What is the most likely cause?
options: A resin or printing parameters problem
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Surface defects are often due to a resin problem or unsuitable printing parameters.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must print a model for a multiple implant case. What printing resolution is recommended?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'A resolution of 50 microns is recommended for multiple implant models to guarantee the precision of positions.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid has printed a model for an orthodontic aligner. Dr Samia asks him to check the finishes. What is the recommended finishing step?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Surface polishing is recommended to obtain a smooth and precise model for aligner manufacturing.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must manage a 3D printing case with complex supports. Dr Rachid advises her to check a parameter. What is this parameter?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Support density is a critical parameter for prints with complex supports.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must choose a 3D printer for his practice. Which criterion is the most important for clinical use?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Precision and surface quality are the most important criteria for clinical use.'

questions.question: Dr Samia has printed a surgical guide but the fit is not perfect. Dr Rachid suggests she check one element. What is this element?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'The quality of the initial scan is often the cause of poor fit of the surgical guide.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid must train his assistant in the use of the 3D printer. What is the first safety rule to teach?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Wearing gloves and protective glasses is essential for handling photopolymer resins.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must manage a case of non-polymerized photopolymer resin. Dr Rachid asks her to check a parameter. What is this parameter?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'The UV exposure time is a critical parameter for the complete polymerization of the resin.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid has printed a model for a complex case. Dr Samia asks him to check the surface condition. What is the importance of the surface condition?
options: It influences the precision of the restoration
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'The surface condition of the model directly influences the precision of the prosthetic restoration.'

questions.question: Dr Samia must choose a resin for printing working models. Which characteristic is the most important?
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Dimensional stability is essential for working models to guarantee the precision of restorations.'

questions.question: Dr Rachid has printed a surgical guide but air bubbles appeared. Dr Samia explains the cause. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Dr Samia explains: 'Air bubbles in the resin are often the cause of bubbles in printed parts.'

questions.question: Dr Samia, after overcoming many 3D printing challenges, receives congratulations from Dr Rachid. What is the next step for Dr Samia?
options: Become a reference in dental 3D printing
questions.explanation: Dr Rachid explains: 'Becoming a reference in dental 3D printing is the next step to share her expertise.'
